questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The choice of Monash University as my study destination was based on its strong academic standing in Economics, Econometrics and Finance, offering tailored elective courses that aligned with my academic goals. The university's diverse campus environment and the appeal of experiencing Australias unique culture were key factors influencing my decision.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Upon arriving late at Monash University, I found the institution to be exceptionally helpful with the onboarding process. Despite my delayed arrival, the university's well-organized support systems, orientation sessions, and online resources efficiently assisted me in accessing essential information about academics, campus facilities, accommodation, and student services.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Upon my arrival at Monash University, I received assistance through an onboarding session tailored for new students. I also had the chance to take a campus tour, which helped me get acquainted with the university facilities and layout.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: None

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found off-campus housing through EasyLiving Melbourne, which offers rentals at discounted rates specifically for international students. Alternatively, I recommend seeking apartments with housemates through platforms like Facebook, as student accommodation tends to be costly.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Living off campus in Melbourne offers a fantastic experience, particularly in vibrant areas like Saint Kilda, Brunswick, South Yarra, Prahran, or Fitzroy. These locations provide an incredible opportunity to immerse oneself in the heart of Melbourne's dynamic lifestyle. Each area has its unique charm and offerings, from eclectic cafes to cultural events, vibrant nightlife, and diverse communities.

Saint Kilda, known for its beautiful beach and lively atmosphere, is perfect for those seeking a laid-back yet vibrant lifestyle. Brunswick and Fitzroy offer an artsy and bohemian vibe with an abundance of trendy cafes, artistic spaces, and a bustling music scene. South Yarra and Prahran boast a mix of upscale living, fashionable boutiques, and vibrant dining options.

Living in these areas not only puts you in close proximity to the university but also allows you to explore Melbourne's diverse culture, events, and attractions. 

I WOULD HIGHLY RECOMEND LIVING OFF-CAMPUS!

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Firstly, for an Australian visa, an online university registration is required, so it's essential to complete this promptly. At Monash University, the registration process involves orientation sessions on university policies, academic requirements, and available resources. Subsequently, students utilize an online portal to select their courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Monash University has a specialized department that offers support to incoming foreign students. They provide guidance on visas, accommodations, course registration, and orientation.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Registering for the classes I wanted went smoothly without any issues.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Plan early

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Courses are much more applied than what i was used to at Copenhagen University.

questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took courses which were MA or Ph.d.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style at my host institution differed notably from UCPH. Monash University's courses were more applied compared to what I was accustomed to at Copenhagen University. For instance, while assignments throughout the semester focused on applied econometrics, the end-of-term exams primarily tested theoretical knowledge.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer:
International Economics
Bank Lending
Macroeconometrics
Applied Derivatives

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I highly recommend the course "Applied Derivatives" to future exchange students. Despite its challenging nature, this course was incredibly rewarding, providing the most learning and enjoyment during my exchange. The practical application of derivatives in this course offered a valuable learning experience, making it both intellectually stimulating and enjoyable.

questions.answer: I encountered no noteworthy unexpected costs during my time abroad.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: In Australia, regular food shopping has become more expensive compared to just a year ago. Housing costs were also higher than anticipated. However, eating out and enjoying coffee at cafes is relatively cheaper compared to Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: At Monash University, students had access to diverse cultural events, athletic facilities with sports activities and fitness classes. The university hosted social gatherings, movie nights, and networking events. Additionally, volunteering and community service opportunities were available.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't attend any non-academic activities during my exchange :)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend visiting students to explore both the city of Melbourne and its beautiful natural surroundings during weekends or holidays. Melbourne offers a vibrant cultural scene, including museums, art galleries, diverse cuisine, and bustling markets to explore. Additionally, the natural landscapes surrounding Melbourne, such as the Great Ocean Road, Yarra Valley wineries, and nearby national parks, offer stunning scenery and outdoor activities for a refreshing break from city life. Consider using services like Turo or Uber Car Share to easily hire cars for trips outside the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Adapting to the local culture at my exchange site was very easy. Australia being an English-speaking country with cultural similarities to Europe in general facilitated a smooth adjustment for me.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I mainly socialized with Danish students abroad, so no. But international student are usually very willing to meet new people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find any cultural differences particularly challenging during my time in Australia. Australians are quite similar to urban Danes, although I noticed that they tended to be more outgoing and initiate conversations more frequently.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The aspect of the culture that I most appreciated was the friendly and non-judgmental attitude of the people. I found that individuals generally behaved kindly and were open-minded, creating a welcoming and accepting atmosphere.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Take time to explore not only the university but also the city of Melbourne and its surrounding areas. Venture out to experience the vibrant city life, beautiful natural landscapes, and diverse cultural offerings that the region has to offer.
AND LIVE OUTSIDE CAMPUS!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: None that i havent already mentioned.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding aspects of my exchange experience were the valuable learning opportunities and the overall experience of living abroad. Both aspects enriched my perspective, allowed personal growth, and provided memorable experiences that I cherish.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge during my exchange was finding housing. Initially, I stayed at an Airbnb for the first two weeks until I secured accommodation. I highly recommend starting the search for private housing months in advance. Personally, I started my search only a month before arriving in Melbourne, which proved to be insufficient time. Starting the housing search early can alleviate the stress of finding accommodation upon arrival.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I hope you get the chance of going to Melbourne on exchange :)!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
